title: Completeness for a second ideal from completeness of a quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and let $I,J\subseteq R$ be ideals. Suppose $R$ is $I$-adically complete and $R/I$ is complete for the image $(I+J)/I$ of $J$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Then $R$ is $J$-adically complete.

proof.text: Put $K=I+J$ and let $c:R\to B=\varprojlim_nR/K^n$ be its canonical completion map. By the Noetherian-ring definition, $K$, $I$ and $J$ are finitely generated. The completion-mod-ideal theorem makes $B$ $KB$-adically complete. Apply the finite-module completion theorem to the cyclic $R$-module $R/I$: its $K$-adic completion is $B\otimes_R(R/I)$. The elementary isomorphism $B\otimes_R(R/I)\cong B/IB$ sends $b\otimes\bar r$ to $bc(r)\bmod IB$, with inverse $b\bmod IB\mapsto b\otimes1$. Also $K^n(R/I)=((I+J)/I)^n(R/I)$. The assumed quotient completeness thus identifies the canonical map $R/I\to B/IB$ with an isomorphism. The tensor theorem’s formula shows this identification sends $\bar r$ to $c(r)\bmod IB$.

source.place: Tag 0DYC, first two sentences; Tags 05GG and 00MA(3).

proof.text: The ideal $IB$ is finitely generated by the images of any finite generators of $I$, and $IB\subseteq KB$. Apply [lem-sfb-adic-complete-subideal] in the ring $B$: it is $IB$-adically complete, hence $\bigcap_n I^nB=0$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-ring] applies to $M=B$ over $R$: $R$ is $I$-complete by hypothesis, the intersection is zero, and $B/IB\cong R/I$ is cyclic. Therefore $B$ is a finite $R$-module.

By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical], every maximal ideal of $R$ contains $I$. Let $C=B/c(R)$ as an $R$-module. It is finite, since the images of finite generators of $B$ generate $C$. The surjectivity of $R/I\to B/IB$ says $B=c(R)+IB$, so $IC=C$. Nakayama gives $C=0$. Thus $c$ is surjective.

The Noetherian completion-flat theorem makes $B$ flat over $R$. For any maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$, $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, and $B/\mathfrak mB\cong (B/IB)/\mathfrak m(B/IB)\cong R/\mathfrak m\ne0$, using the $R$-linear quotient identification from step 1. Thus the maximal-ideal criterion makes $B$ faithfully flat over $R$. Faithfully flat ideal contraction at the zero ideal gives injectivity of $c$. Together with step 3, $c$ is bijective.

source.place: Tag 0DYC, flatness and faithful-flatness sentences; Tags 00MB, 00HP and 05CK.

proof.text: The bijectivity of the canonical $K$-completion map is exactly $K$-adic completeness of $R$. Since $J\subseteq K$ and $J$ is finitely generated, [lem-sfb-adic-complete-subideal] applied in $R$ gives the required $J$-adic completeness.
